This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal has been filed Challenging the award passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal(Special District Court No.1), at Cuddalore, made in M.C.O.P.No.398 of 2017 dated 08.01.2024.
2.

sentences.text: The respondents/claimants 1 and 2 filed a claim petition under Section 166(1)(a) of the Tamil Nadu Motor Accident Claims Tribunal rules and claiming a compensation of Rs.2,00,00,000/- for the death of 1st respondent's husband and the son of the 2nd respondent in a road accident.

entities.text: Tamil Nadu Motor Accident Claims Tribunal
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. The learned Tribunal after hearing both sides and upon considering the oral and documentary evidence has granted compensation Rs.76,85,000/- in the following manner:-
Sl.No Description
1 . For loss of income  https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 21/07/2025 07:23:2

Sl.No Description   
 2. For love and affection   3. For funeral expenses   4. For Transportation   5. Loss of Estate   Total   Rounded  4. The Tribunal has directed the appellant to pay the compensation to the respondents 1 and 2 with interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a.
5. The appellant/Insurance Company, not being satisfied with the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, has filed this appeal to set aside the findings of the Tribunal.
6. The learned counsel appearing for the appellant/Insurance Company submitted that the the deceased was driven his two wheeler in a rash and negligent manner due to which the accident was happened.
He further submitted that the 3rd respondent's car was proceeding from Mayiladuthurai to Panruti.

At that time, one tanker lorry whose https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
21/07/2025 07:23:24 pm ) registration number is not known came in the opposite direction dashed against the front right side of the 3rd respondent's car and thereby, the front right tyre has been removed due to which, the 3rd respondent's car was totally damaged in the right front portion, the The Divisional Manager vs R.Kasturi on 6 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33098560/
2 tanker lorry driver still later dashed against the deceased's motorcycle and ran away from the place of accident.
Therefore, the 3rd respondent's car is not responsible for the accident and the appellant is not liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, he prayed to set aside the findings of the Tribunal 7.
The learned counsel for the respondents 1 and 2 submitted that based on the salary certificate of the deceased was produced on the side of the claimants Ex.P8.
Therefore the Tribunal has rightly fixed the compensation and there is no negligent on the part of the deceased.
Hence, the award passed by the Tribunal is reasonable one.

8. On considering the both submissions and on perusal of the records, it reveals that accident was happened in the year 2016 and the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 21/07/2025 07:23:24 pm ) deceased had driven the vehicle from the opposite direction.
Furthe, the deceased's salary certificate was produced by the claimants (Ex.P8) and the same was rightly awarded by the Tribunal.
However, the Tribunal has not deducted the income tax amount.
Therefore, this Court is inclined to deduct the income tax amount of 10 % from the award under the head of loss of income comes around Rs.67,99,518.
Therefore, the loss of income awarded by the Tribunal is reduced from Rs.75,55,020/- to 67,99,518/-.
Accordingly, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal to the claimant is re-
quantified as follows'-.

For love and Rs.80,000/- Rs.
 affection  3. For funeral expenses Rs.15,000/- Rs.
 4. For Transportation Rs.10,000/- Rs.
 5. Loss of property Rs.25,000/- Rs.
In the result, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

(
Uploaded on: 21/07/2025 07:23:24 pm ) and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal at Rs.76,85,020/- is hereby reduced to Rs.69,29,518/- together with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of deposit.

The appellant is directed to deposit the entire award amount now determined by this Court along with interest, less the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this Judgment,
to the credit of M.C.O.P.No.398 of 2017 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal(Special District Court No.1), at Cuddalore.
